newsitem.title: DENMARK: INTERVIEW-Novo Nordisk to cut air freight.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Novo Nordisk to cut air freight.

text.p: Danish biotech group Novo Nordisk, a major shipper of goods by air from Denmark, said it plans to cut down the volume of its air freight shipments and would substitute them with cheaper alternatives.

"We have established our own production in the U.S., South Africa, Japan, China and France which means total volume of goods shipped internationally will decrease somewhat from Denmark over the coming years," said Carsten Kristensen, head of the shipping department for the company's health care division.

About 75 percent of the division's total distribution costs were for air freight, he said. The company's biggest markets were the Far East, the U.S., Japan and Australia but Novo Nordisk ships its pharmaceuticals all over the world.
He said he expected the U.S. market to be supplied from the company's production plant in North Carolina and that supply to Europe would be from a production facility outside Paris.

The company's health care division shipped around 1.7 million kg by air in 1996, 3.2 million kg by truck and 630,000 kg by ship. In 1997 Kristensen said he expected volumes shipped by air freight for the unit to remain about the same.
He said at the end of 1996 the health care division's average freight cost was around six Danish crowns per kg, based on average air, sea and trucking costs.
"This relates to increased volumes shipped by sea. In 1994 all three freight rates gave an average cost per kg of seven crowns and that was based on heavy quantities shipped by air," Kristensen said.
He said the company had recently introduced a global auto-management system. Its affiliates could place orders directly in the system.
"We have more control of the whole supply chain," he said.
He said the company's image as an air freight shipper would probably be reduced as the volumes shipped by air level fell and it sought ways to cut urgent shipments.

"The total volumes shipped are increasing and they will increase further. The volumes shipped by air stabilised in 1994, '95 and '96 so they are almost the same. The figures for 1997 will also be the same," he said.

He said other business areas were switching away from air freight. "Within the enzymes business we are trying to reduce the use of air freight and turn more towards sea freight and trucking within Europe."
Shipments to Russia have increased considerably in the past few years. Novo Nordisk is Russia's largest supplier of insulin, the company said.
The company uses trucking companies to Russia and the Ukraine and but also air shipments because it is a way to avoid red tape.
In general, the company would remain a user of air freight because not all of its sensitive -- sometimes extremely expensive products -- are suitable to go by any other way.

"We will still have to air freight for smaller shipments not fit for sea freight. Most orders for direct customers, non affiliates or agents, will also be shipped by air because of the size," he said.
